source_text:
(7) Στίχ.ι΄. Ἆρά γε ἐλθόντες ἐλευσόμεθα ἐγώ τεκαὶ ἡ μήτηρ σου, καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί σου προσκυνῆσαί σοι ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν;
Σαφῶς ἡ μήτηρ τοῦ Ἰωσὴφ πρὸ τῶν ἐνυπνίων ἐτελεύτησεν. Μήποτε οὖν δυνάμεθα τὴν Μαριὰμ καὶ τὸν Ἰωσὴφ εἰπεῖν προφητεύεσθαι προσκυνήσειν τῷ Χριστῷ;
thought_title: Joseph's dream about his mother and brothers bowing
orientation: Origen is commenting on Joseph's dream in Genesis 37:10, where Joseph's father asks whether he, Joseph's mother, and his brothers will come to bow down to him.
pass_a_gloss: [Is it] indeed [that] having come we will come, I and your mother, and your brothers, to bow down to you upon the earth? Clearly the mother of Joseph died before the dreams. Perhaps therefore are we able to say [that] Mary and Joseph are prophesied [as] going to bow down to Christ?

choices.why: The particle ἆρα with γε marks a question expecting reflection; 'indeed' preserves the force of γε.
The participle plus finite verb is a Semitic-style emphatic construction; the literal rendering keeps the doubling visible.

choices.english: to bow down to you upon the earth
choices.why: The phrase 'upon the earth' specifies prostration to the ground; 'earth' rather than 'ground' keeps the biblical register.
rejected: to worship you on the ground

choices.why: Μήποτε introduces a tentative suggestion; οὖν marks the inference from the mother's death.

choices.english: are prophesied as going to bow down to
choices.why: The passive infinitive plus future infinitive construction is rendered with 'as going to' to show the predicted action.
rejected: are prophesied that they will bow

bible_refs.note: Ἆρά γε ἐλθόντες ἐλευσόμεθα ἐγώ τε καὶ ἡ μήτηρ σου, καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί σου προσκυνῆσαί σοι ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν;

pass_b_english: “Is it indeed that I and your mother and your brothers will come and bow down to you upon the earth?” (Genesis 37:10). Joseph’s mother clearly died before the dreams. Perhaps, then, we can say that Mary and Joseph are prophesied as going to bow down to Christ?
